removability.rationale: Deleting a feature means removing a route directory, one data function and one section block; no scattered references, no dead code left behind. Not a pure 'delete dir + nav link' because the Pokémon page section and its data builder must also go.

app/src/lib/format.ts — by contrast, naming/dex/flavor rules are centralized and single-sourced
changeability.rationale: Most fixes land in one obvious place (format.ts, api.ts, move-table.tsx), but card construction is duplicated across three sites with two sprite-derivation strategies, so the sprite-class bug must be fixed twice and the sites must be discovered first.

app/src/lib/team.ts:24-26 — comment explains cookie attributes duplicated to keep the module browser-safe

coupling.rationale: Clean layering with explicit, documented server/client seams and narrow interfaces; the only tangles are the monolithic data.ts hub and one shared global.css.

evidence: app/src/lib/data.ts:72-86 — cardsForPokemon's `extra` callback handles the hidden-ability variation without flag params
app/src/components/ui.tsx:16-40 — PokemonCard/CardList reused by home, move, ability, type and team pages
app/src/components/move-table.tsx:11-20 — COLUMNS/sort generic over MoveRow; level column varies by method, not by boolean prop at call sites
app/src/routes/moves/[name]/index.tsx — a Moves-shaped page is a thin route over one data function, so an Items clone reuses Section/CardList/orDash/NotFound wholesale
abstraction_design.rationale: Abstractions track the app's real variation well and stretch to a new resource section with near-total reuse; only the home page's inline Card construction is a copy of an existing pattern.

findings.issue: Card sprite derivation duplicated: homePage and cardsForPokemon each synthesize spriteUrl(id) while teamPage uses the fetched pokemon.sprites.front_default — a sprite bug (e.g. wrong sprite when a species' default Pokémon differs) needs fixing in two sites and the home one needs a default-variety lookup
findings.suggestion: Route all Card construction through one helper that resolves the species' default Pokémon sprite (fetch or derive it in one place), and have homePage use it too

findings.issue: Single 430-line module holds every page's data builder (homePage, pokemonPage, movePage, abilityPage, typesPage, typePage, teamPage); edit conflicts and 'where does X live' cost grow with each new resource
findings.suggestion: Split into per-resource modules (lib/data/pokemon.ts, moves.ts, …) keeping shared helpers (speciesById, typeRef, cardsForPokemon) in a common module

findings.issue: All styles for every page live in one global stylesheet with comment-sectioned regions; Qwik supports per-component scoped styles, so removing or adding a page means editing a shared file under one namespace
findings.suggestion: Use Qwik's scoped styles (import './x.css' in the component) for page-specific rules, keeping tokens and shared component styles global

findings.issue: homePage re-implements Card construction (humanize + spriteUrl) instead of reusing cardsForPokemon, the second copy of that pattern
findings.suggestion: Extract a cardFromSpecies helper and share it between homePage and cardsForPokemon

findings.issue: Starter-template leftovers: `engines-annotation` about sharp (no sharp dependency) and an `undici: "*"` devDependency not imported anywhere in src/
findings.suggestion: Drop the unused annotation and dependency to keep package.json honest about real constraints

findings.issue: homeHref/filter helpers are route-local, which is fine today, but any second page needing these filters (e.g. an /items list) would copy them
findings.suggestion: If a filtered list pattern recurs, move the query-string filter helpers into lib/format or a small lib/filters module

summary: This is a well-structured Qwik City app with thin routes over a server-only data layer, narrow typed component props, and deliberate attention to the server/client seam — most changes land in one obvious place. The main editability cost is duplicated Card construction in data.ts (three sites, two sprite strategies), which makes the sprite-bug class of fix a two-place change. Styling in one global CSS file and a monolithic data.ts are mild scaling concerns, not blockers.
